title: yoga nidra
hook: Vishnu sleeps on the cosmic waters, two demons rise to kill Brahma, and Brahma has to wake him
carry: the goddess who holds the sleep

segments.voice: Yesterday closed mantra sadhana with Patanjali: practice grows firm through a long time, no break, with care.
screen: `MANTRA SADHANA.` · `A LONG TIME. NO BREAK. WITH CARE.`

segments.voice: Everything is water. One age of the world has ended, and the next hasn't begun. On that ocean, on the coils of a great serpent, Vishnu lies asleep. From his navel rises a lotus, and on the lotus sits Brahma, the one who will make the next world. Then two demons, Madhu and Kaitabha, rise out of the dark and come for Brahma. He looks down at the one person who could help him, and Vishnu doesn't stir. This sleep isn't ordinary. It has a name, and the name is today's word.
screen: `ONE OCEAN. VISHNU ASLEEP.` → `TWO DEMONS COME FOR BRAHMA.` → `THE SLEEP HAS A NAME.`

segments.voice: The story opens the Devi Mahatmya, the Glory of the Goddess, a text set inside the Markandeya Purana. Brahma doesn't shake Vishnu. He doesn't shout. He turns to the power that is holding Vishnu asleep, and he praises her. The text calls her Yoganidra. Yoga nidra: the sleep of yoga. In this story she isn't a technique. She is the Goddess herself, the great power behind creation, its keeping and its ending, and Vishnu's sleep is one of her forms. Brahma's hymn calls her by many names, among them the great night and the night of delusion, and also intelligence and understanding. Then he asks her to let Vishnu go. And she does. The text says she withdraws from his eyes, his mouth, his nose, his arms, his heart and his chest, and the Lord of the world rises. He fights Madhu and Kaitabha, and in the end they're undone. So the first thing yoga nidra carries, on this path, is a picture: a sleep that isn't absence. Vishnu isn't knocked out. He rests on the waters, held by a power so great that even the creator has to ask her leave to wake him. In the coming days this idea runs into the Upanishads, into Patanjali, and into the guided practice people now do lying on a mat. But it begins here, on the water.
screen: `BRAHMA PRAISES THE ONE WHO HOLDS THE SLEEP.` · `YOGANIDRA IS THE GODDESS HERSELF.` · `SHE LEAVES HIS EYES, HIS HEART. HE RISES.` · `A SLEEP THAT ISN'T ABSENCE.` · then, large: `YOGA NIDRA: THE SLEEP OF YOGA.`

segments.voice: Lie down, or lean back in your chair, and let the body be heavy, as if resting on water. Follow the story's waking slowly, in reverse: the chest rising and falling, the heart, the arms resting, the nose with the breath moving in it, the mouth soft, the eyes still behind the lids. Don't try to sleep and don't try to stay alert; just rest and notice.
Yoga nidra. The sleep of yoga. In the Devi Mahatmya, it's the Goddess herself, holding Vishnu asleep on the waters.
Your line: the goddess who holds the sleep. A sleep so full it has its own hymn. That's day one thousand nineteen.

howItsDone: Hindus who recite the Devi Mahatmya, especially during Navaratri, read Brahma's hymn to Yoganidra in its first chapter; some temples and households chant the whole text over several days.
